blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

  BUMP --> P[publish gate: check_changelog_size.sh]

# gh-1452: Release blocked: CHANGELOG.md exceeds pub.dev 256 KiB cap (262 672 B on main) — v1.0.538 not on pub.dev; trim + pre-flight guard needed

## Description

## Release blocked: CHANGELOG.md crossed pub.dev's 256 KiB content cap — v1.0.538 on GitHub but NOT on pub.dev

### Facts (verified)
- CI run **37935837870** (ev=push, v1.0.538 tag push by fa-release-bot) FAILED 13:35:47Z; single failed job `Publish to pub.dev` (113844282424): `dart pub publish --force` server-rejected at upload — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes).` All other legs green (PTY shards, gates, ratchets, binaries, signing).
- `CHANGELOG.md` on origin/main = **262 672 bytes** — 528 bytes over the cap; the v1.0.538 entry is what crossed it.
- Consequence: GitHub release v1.0.538 exists (13:17:52Z) but **pub.dev has no 1.0.538**. The workflow's own manual-publish fallback (see #554) did not engage — the job died at the upload step itself.
- The serialized release-event twin (37935839275) is expected to hit the same server reject — same incident, one triage.
- No auto-triage issue was filed by the release-CI red path (as of 13:50Z).

### Mechanism
The changelog is append-only by convention (one entry per publish, repo rules) and the bot releases near-daily (536→538 within two days); nothing bounds its size anywhere: no repo lint, no release-workflow pre-flight, no `dart pub publish --dry-run` size signal. pub.dev's hard cap was therefore inevitable and was discovered at the worst possible point — after tag, after GitHub release, mid-upload.

### Ask (machine lanes)
1. **Trim/archive CHANGELOG.md on main** as its own CHANGELOG-only commit (no version bump): keep a bounded recent window inline (e.g. last ~30 versions) and archive the tail to `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` (or drop it entirely — GitHub releases already carry full history). Target comfortably under 200 KiB.
2. Next release cycle (v1.0.539+) then publishes clean; **v1.0.538 stays GitHub-release-only** (skip-version precedent: v1.0.537 already skipped; pub.dev simply misses it) — do NOT re-tag/move v1.0.538.
3. **Add a fast-fail guard**: release workflow (and/or repo lint) asserts `CHANGELOG.md < 262144 bytes` BEFORE tag/publish, so the next approach of the cap surfaces pre-tag, not mid-upload.

### Non-goals
No CI dispatch/retry from agents (CI-DISPATCH BAN); no protocol/workflow redesign beyond the pre-flight check; no backfill publish of 1.0.538 via manual path unless explicitly ordered (blocked by the same oversized file anyway until the trim lands).

### References
- Failed run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37935837870 (job 113844282424)
- GitHub release v1.0.538 (out) vs pub.dev (missing 1.0.538); twin 37935839275 (ev=release).
- Sibling release-flow defects this week: #1442 (red-intake no-op), #1448 (fa-state citation integrity) — machine bookkeeping/release integrity family.
- Manual-publish fallback reference: #554.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#    is PAT-pushed annotated (release-tag/auto_release), so the push twin

    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.

    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."

          fi

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Both test files pass. Now the exhaustive pass — remaining checks:

1. **Exact-cap semantics**: pub.dev message says "exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)". The actual pub.dev validation: `CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — I believe pub.dev rejects when size > 262144? Or >=? Actually pub.dev's backend limit: tar content max per file... The ticket itself says "asserts CHANGELOG.md < 262144 bytes" — the PR implements strict less-than which matches the ticket AC. Conservative direction (fails earlier). Fine.

2. **check_changelog_size.sh portability**: `size=$(wc -c < "$file")` — on macOS/BSD wc produces leading spaces; `[ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]` in bash handles leading whitespace integer comparison? Actually bash's `[` with `-ge` does integer comparison after trimming? The POSIX test does strtol which skips leading whitespace — yes, works. But `echo "$file: $size bytes"` would print extra spaces — cosmetic. The release sandbox tests run on ubuntu CI anyway. Minor at most. Actually wait — is `size` used in the message: "::error::$file is $size bytes" — with leading spaces it'd be "CHANGELOG.md is  100 bytes". Cosmetic only. Not worth flagging beyond maybe a suggestion. Actually, `$(...)` strips trailing newlines but not leading spaces. In bash, `[ " 100" -ge 100 ]` → works (test builtin uses arithmetic evaluation that tolerates whitespace). OK, skip or mention as nit. Probably skip — CI is ubuntu.

3. **Guard in auto_release.sh placement within retry loop**: when the guard fails, `set -euo pipefail` aborts the whole script with exit 1 — no retry loop swallow. Confirmed `set -e` at line 26. Good. But wait — the guard is inside `for attempt in 1 2 3`; on failure the script exits (set -e). Good.

4. **Does auto_release.sh run from repo root?** The script does `git reset --hard origin/main` and operates on relative paths (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md) — it already assumes cwd=repo root; the guard uses the same convention as the existing `bash scripts/...` invocation? Let me check how check_lockfiles.sh is invoked in auto_release.sh to confirm the same pattern.

5. **CHANGELOG.md new header** — the trimmed file has a prose preamble; the auto_release python rewrite looks for `^## Unreleased` and inserts the release section at its position, replacing the curated Unreleased content. With the new preamble, the rewrite still works (Unreleased is at the end, line 246). The release entries order: new section replaces Unreleased content in place — since Unreleased is last, new version sections appear before... wait: the python inserts the new section where `## Unreleased` was, then re-appends `## Unreleased` at the end. New versions will accumulate between the last archived-window version and Unreleased. Order stays ascending. Good.

But — subtle: the trimmed file's newest release is 1.0.541 at the bottom (before Unreleased). The header preamble at the top mentions the archive. All fine.

6. **Pubspec/CHANGELOG consistency**: CHANGELOG trimmed keeps "## 1.0.506 → 1.0.541" — current version on branch? pubspec version: v1.0.541 was just committed in the merge (c7a5e0b6d chore(release): v1.0.541). pubspec on HEAD = 1.0.541? Check that pubspec.yaml version matches the top changelog entry — pub.dev shows changelog; if the newest entry is missing it warns but doesn't block. Not an issue.

7. **Line numbers for inline comments**: need diff lines. The changed files:
   - .github/workflows/ci.yml (+5 at ~2876-2880)
   - scripts/check_changelog_size.sh (new file, lines 1-39)
   - scripts/auto_release.sh (+8 at ~127-134)
   - test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart (new, 120 lines)
   - test/release_hygiene_test.dart (+44)
   - CHANGELOG.md / CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (content moves)

Findings so far — mostly positive. Any real issues?

a) **SUGGESTION**: temp dir leak in test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart — `_tmpRoot` never cleaned up (addTearDown). Compare: does release_hygiene_test clean up? It also uses `_fixtureRoot` without cleanup — established pattern. So not worth flagging; consistent with existing pattern.

b) **`wc -c` leading whitespace portability** — skip (consistent with GNU-only assumptions; auto_release.sh already requires GNU sed -i per the fixture comment "CI-authored, ubuntu").

c) **IMPORTANT?**: The archive split — is the boundary right? Archive contains everything before 1.0.506 including... archive ends at "## 1.0.505"? Let me check the tail of the archive. Also confirm no version appears in both files.

d) **Missing guard on other root-package publish path?** Is there any other workflow that publishes the root package? We checked: ci.yml publish job (covered), nightly (dry-run), publish-fa-llm (different package). What about manual publish fallback (#554)? That's inside the same publish job presumably. Covered.

e) **The `repo CHANGELOG.md is under the cap` test** is a good ratchet but note: test runs from repo root via `File('CHANGELOG.md')` — dart test cwd is package root. Fine.

f) One consideration: **the trimmed CHANGELOG.md preamble is 8 lines of prose** — pub.dev renders the changelog; fine.

g) **ci.yml gate**: the guard runs in the `gate` step even for... the publish job only fires on tag pushes. Fine. But note the gate step doesn't checkout with full history — irrelevant for wc -c.

h) **`check_changelog_size.sh` in the ci.yml publish job**: runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` from repo root after checkout — file exists. Good.

i) **Edge**: `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` exit code propagates through the run block — the block has no `set -e` but GitHub Actions run steps use `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` by default, so a failing command fails the step. Good.

And `git add pubspec.yaml` — first occurrence line 153. Guard at 133. Between: the python rewrite ends at PY line ~125, guard at 133. Correct.

n) **The Unreleased-section duplication risk**: python rewrite appends "## Unreleased" if missing. With trimmed changelog having Unreleased at end — fine.

o) One more check — **`stage_publish_package.sh`**: the publish job stages the package then publishes from the stage. Does the staged copy include CHANGELOG.md? The gate runs the guard on the repo-root CHANGELOG.md before staging. Staged copy presumably copies CHANGELOG.md. Fine.

I am 50-50% on this, maybe slightly to concur: I think we should rather keep the current limit.

One part is Datastore: besides the single entity limit, we also have an overall transaction limit, and at upload time we write a lot of entries in a single transaction. (We could separate the content extraction from the main transaction though, but that introduces an additional backfill process).

The other part is the sheer size: the current changelog for `flex_color_scheme` is 40+ pages. It is impressively detailed, but I doubt that users of v5.1 are interested in changes that happened 1.5+ years ago in v1.3.

I think we should figure out how these files could grow and how they should be displayed. Maybe we need to customize the content extraction of the changelog, and display only the last-N versions (or up until 128 Kb). That way the input file could keep its size, and we also limit the size to the common query patterns.

Key confirmation: pub.dev's 256 KiB cap applies to **README.md and CHANGELOG.md specifically** (the rendering content), not arbitrary files. So `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` shipping in the package is NOT going to hit that cap. It only contributes total archive size (~247 KB of 100 MB cap — negligible). So the "archive will regrow" concern is not a publish blocker. It's arguably still worth excluding from the publish payload to keep packages lean, but that's at most a SUGGESTION, and there's a guarded mirror between .pubignore and stage_publish_package.sh that would need coordinated changes + test updates. I'll flag it as a SUGGESTION... actually is it even worth it? 247KB in a ~32MB archive. Marginal. But the archive will grow indefinitely (append-only trims). Over years it could reach MBs. Still small. I could mention it as an optional note in the general comment rather than an inline comment. Let me decide: SUGGESTION inline on CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md addition line? The diff for CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md — new file; inline comment line 1. It is in the PR diff (added lines). I can attach there.

1. **PR description drift**: says "keeps the last 30 versions (1.0.506 → 1.0.540)" but actually keeps 31 versions (1.0.506→1.0.541, main advanced). Cosmetic only — skip or general note.

2. **Guard script — `wc -c < "$file"` in command substitution**: fine on GNU. The script targets CI/ubuntu (release pipeline) — consistent with auto_release.sh's existing GNU-sed assumption. Skip.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

I am 50-50% on this, maybe slightly to concur: I think we should rather keep the current limit.

One part is Datastore: besides the single entity limit, we also have an overall transaction limit, and at upload time we write a lot of entries in a single transaction. (We could separate the content extraction from the main transaction though, but that introduces an additional backfill process).

The other part is the sheer size: the current changelog for `flex_color_scheme` is 40+ pages. It is impressively detailed, but I doubt that users of v5.1 are interested in changes that happened 1.5+ years ago in v1.3.

I think we should figure out how these files could grow and how they should be displayed. Maybe we need to customize the content extraction of the changelog, and display only the last-N versions (or up until 128 Kb). That way the input file could keep its size, and we also limit the size to the common query patterns.

- Guard measured post-entry in `auto_release.sh`, so the abort happens before tag_release/publish can fire — the approach of the cap now surfaces pre-tag, not mid-upload (the v1.0.538 failure point).

  BUMP --> P[publish gate: check_changelog_size.sh]
  P -->|ok| PUB[dart pub publish]
  P -->|over cap| FF[fail before upload]
```

</details>

# gh-1452: Release blocked: CHANGELOG.md exceeds pub.dev 256 KiB cap (262 672 B on main) — v1.0.538 not on pub.dev; trim + pre-flight guard needed

## Description

## Release blocked: CHANGELOG.md crossed pub.dev's 256 KiB content cap — v1.0.538 on GitHub but NOT on pub.dev

### Facts (verified)
- CI run **37935837870** (ev=push, v1.0.538 tag push by fa-release-bot) FAILED 13:35:47Z; single failed job `Publish to pub.dev` (113844282424): `dart pub publish --force` server-rejected at upload — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes).` All other legs green (PTY shards, gates, ratchets, binaries, signing).
- `CHANGELOG.md` on origin/main = **262 672 bytes** — 528 bytes over the cap; the v1.0.538 entry is what crossed it.
- Consequence: GitHub release v1.0.538 exists (13:17:52Z) but **pub.dev has no 1.0.538**. The workflow's own manual-publish fallback (see #554) did not engage — the job died at the upload step itself.
- The serialized release-event twin (37935839275) is expected to hit the same server reject — same incident, one triage.
- No auto-triage issue was filed by the release-CI red path (as of 13:50Z).

### Mechanism
The changelog is append-only by convention (one entry per publish, repo rules) and the bot releases near-daily (536→538 within two days); nothing bounds its size anywhere: no repo lint, no release-workflow pre-flight, no `dart pub publish --dry-run` size signal. pub.dev's hard cap was therefore inevitable and was discovered at the worst possible point — after tag, after GitHub release, mid-upload.

### Ask (machine lanes)
1. **Trim/archive CHANGELOG.md on main** as its own CHANGELOG-only commit (no version bump): keep a bounded recent window inline (e.g. last ~30 versions) and archive the tail to `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` (or drop it entirely — GitHub releases already carry full history). Target comfortably under 200 KiB.
2. Next release cycle (v1.0.539+) then publishes clean; **v1.0.538 stays GitHub-release-only** (skip-version precedent: v1.0.537 already skipped; pub.dev simply misses it) — do NOT re-tag/move v1.0.538.
3. **Add a fast-fail guard**: release workflow (and/or repo lint) asserts `CHANGELOG.md < 262144 bytes` BEFORE tag/publish, so the next approach of the cap surfaces pre-tag, not mid-upload.

### Non-goals
No CI dispatch/retry from agents (CI-DISPATCH BAN); no protocol/workflow redesign beyond the pre-flight check; no backfill publish of 1.0.538 via manual path unless explicitly ordered (blocked by the same oversized file anyway until the trim lands).

### References
- Failed run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37935837870 (job 113844282424)
- GitHub release v1.0.538 (out) vs pub.dev (missing 1.0.538); twin 37935839275 (ev=release).
- Sibling release-flow defects this week: #1442 (red-intake no-op), #1448 (fa-state citation integrity) — machine bookkeeping/release integrity family.
- Manual-publish fallback reference: #554.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

I am 50-50% on this, maybe slightly to concur: I think we should rather keep the current limit.

One part is Datastore: besides the single entity limit, we also have an overall transaction limit, and at upload time we write a lot of entries in a single transaction. (We could separate the content extraction from the main transaction though, but that introduces an additional backfill process).

The other part is the sheer size: the current changelog for `flex_color_scheme` is 40+ pages. It is impressively detailed, but I doubt that users of v5.1 are interested in changes that happened 1.5+ years ago in v1.3.

I think we should figure out how these files could grow and how they should be displayed. Maybe we need to customize the content extraction of the changelog, and display only the last-N versions (or up until 128 Kb). That way the input file could keep its size, and we also limit the size to the common query patterns.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

Entries before 1.0.506, moved out of `CHANGELOG.md` on 2026-10-09
(gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose `CHANGELOG.md`
exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so the inline file keeps a bounded
recent window and this archive carries the tail. GitHub releases carry
the same history per version.

- feat(providers): issue #1398 — stall-recovery tuning becomes per-provider

  roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries) accept optional
  `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive-int parsing);
===

- feat(1079): SDK slice 6 — IT-5 record-level runtime parity for extension hosts (YoClip scenario) (#1456)
- gh-1449 [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call (#1451)
- gh-1439 [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance) (#1443)

#    is PAT-pushed annotated (release-tag/auto_release), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects the upload when CHANGELOG.md is
          # at/over its 262144-byte content cap (v1.0.538 died mid-upload,
          # after the tag + GitHub release). Fast-fail HERE, before staging
          # and publish, not at the server.
          bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Verify tag matches pubspec version
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag pubspec=$version"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag v$tag does not match pubspec version $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      # the whole job: it exports PUB_TOKEN and registers

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stage the publishable package into a target directory (issue #597).
#
# `dart publish` packs everything under the repo root that isn't
# gitignored — and the root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the
# pub package (flutter_app with its 57 MB wasm toolchain, yoclip media,
# browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs, packages/*). That
# blew the archive past pub.dev's hard 100 MB cap (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB).
#
# The staged copy carries the package surface (~32 MB) plus the two PATH
# dev-dependencies (packages/fa_llm_mock, vendored vendor/xterm —
# accepted by pub.dev since v0.1.369). pubspec_overrides.yaml (the
# local-only dart_tui vendor pin, "never ships to pub.dev" by its own
# comment) must NOT enter the stage: version solving would re-pin the
# path dep and fail (the v0.1.407 failure, exit 66).
#
# Usage: stage_publish_package.sh <target-dir>
# Exits non-zero (with ::error) when the staged tree exceeds the guard.
# The repo root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the pub package
# (flutter_app, yoclip, browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs)
# — `dart publish` packs everything under the root that isn't gitignored
# (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB, over pub.dev's hard cap). Stage the package
# surface instead. PATH dev-deps of the core pubspec must resolve inside
# the stage (#584, `dart pub get` exit 66 on v0.1.407): their subtrees
# are included BEFORE the parent excludes, and the parent excludes are
# child-scoped (vendor/*) — excluding the parent dir itself would prune
# the subtree before the includes are ever consulted.
# pubspec_overrides.yaml is the workspace-only dart_tui pin (never
# published, see its header); shipped into the stage it re-dangles
# dart_tui onto the excluded vendor dir.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

blocks.text:
Both test files pass. Now the exhaustive pass — remaining checks:

1. **Exact-cap semantics**: pub.dev message says "exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)". The actual pub.dev validation: `CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — I believe pub.dev rejects when size > 262144? Or >=? Actually pub.dev's backend limit: tar content max per file... The ticket itself says "asserts CHANGELOG.md < 262144 bytes" — the PR implements strict less-than which matches the ticket AC. Conservative direction (fails earlier). Fine.

2. **check_changelog_size.sh portability**: `size=$(wc -c < "$file")` — on macOS/BSD wc produces leading spaces; `[ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]` in bash handles leading whitespace integer comparison? Actually bash's `[` with `-ge` does integer comparison after trimming? The POSIX test does strtol which skips leading whitespace — yes, works. But `echo "$file: $size bytes"` would print extra spaces — cosmetic. The release sandbox tests run on ubuntu CI anyway. Minor at most. Actually wait — is `size` used in the message: "::error::$file is $size bytes" — with leading spaces it'd be "CHANGELOG.md is  100 bytes". Cosmetic only. Not worth flagging beyond maybe a suggestion. Actually, `$(...)` strips trailing newlines but not leading spaces. In bash, `[ " 100" -ge 100 ]` → works (test builtin uses arithmetic evaluation that tolerates whitespace). OK, skip or mention as nit. Probably skip — CI is ubuntu.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi

    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate

    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

I am 50-50% on this, maybe slightly to concur: I think we should rather keep the current limit.

One part is Datastore: besides the single entity limit, we also have an overall transaction limit, and at upload time we write a lot of entries in a single transaction. (We could separate the content extraction from the main transaction though, but that introduces an additional backfill process).

The other part is the sheer size: the current changelog for `flex_color_scheme` is 40+ pages. It is impressively detailed, but I doubt that users of v5.1 are interested in changes that happened 1.5+ years ago in v1.3.

I think we should figure out how these files could grow and how they should be displayed. Maybe we need to customize the content extraction of the changelog, and display only the last-N versions (or up until 128 Kb). That way the input file could keep its size, and we also limit the size to the common query patterns.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stage the publishable package into a target directory (issue #597).
#
# `dart publish` packs everything under the repo root that isn't
# gitignored — and the root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the
# pub package (flutter_app with its 57 MB wasm toolchain, yoclip media,
# browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs, packages/*). That
# blew the archive past pub.dev's hard 100 MB cap (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB).
#
# The staged copy carries the package surface (~32 MB) plus the two PATH
# dev-dependencies (packages/fa_llm_mock, vendored vendor/xterm —
# accepted by pub.dev since v0.1.369). pubspec_overrides.yaml (the
# local-only dart_tui vendor pin, "never ships to pub.dev" by its own
# comment) must NOT enter the stage: version solving would re-pin the
# path dep and fail (the v0.1.407 failure, exit 66).
#
# Usage: stage_publish_package.sh <target-dir>
# Exits non-zero (with ::error) when the staged tree exceeds the guard.
# The repo root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the pub package
# (flutter_app, yoclip, browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs)
# — `dart publish` packs everything under the root that isn't gitignored
# (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB, over pub.dev's hard cap). Stage the package
# surface instead. PATH dev-deps of the core pubspec must resolve inside
# the stage (#584, `dart pub get` exit 66 on v0.1.407): their subtrees
# are included BEFORE the parent excludes, and the parent excludes are
# child-scoped (vendor/*) — excluding the parent dir itself would prune
# the subtree before the includes are ever consulted.
# pubspec_overrides.yaml is the workspace-only dart_tui pin (never
# published, see its header); shipped into the stage it re-dangles
# dart_tui onto the excluded vendor dir.

name: Publish fa_llm

on:
  push:
    tags: ['fa_llm-v*']

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177).
concurrency:
  group: Publish fa_llm-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
  contents: read

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/fa_llm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Publish to pub.dev
        run: dart pub publish --force===

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);

Good — publish-fa-llm publishes a different package (packages/fa_llm, has its own CHANGELOG presumably), and nightly is dry-run only. So both publish surfaces of the ROOT package are covered.

Now check:
1. instruction.md at repo root (mentioned in guidelines) — actually the instructions say "instruction.md (repo root)". Let me check if it exists.
2. AGENTS.md conventions for shell/tests.
3. Run the new tests to verify they pass.
4. Check release_hygiene_test diff fully (already seen most). Also check `runAutoReleaseDirect` — does it run the real scripts/auto_release.sh from repo root, and how does cwd work with `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md`? The fixture seeds scripts/check_changelog_size.sh into the fixture dir, and runs auto_release.sh with cwd = fixture root. Need to confirm auto_release.sh is also copied into fixture — line 341 context shows they copy check_lockfiles.sh and check_changelog_size.sh. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

I am 50-50% on this, maybe slightly to concur: I think we should rather keep the current limit.

One part is Datastore: besides the single entity limit, we also have an overall transaction limit, and at upload time we write a lot of entries in a single transaction. (We could separate the content extraction from the main transaction though, but that introduces an additional backfill process).

The other part is the sheer size: the current changelog for `flex_color_scheme` is 40+ pages. It is impressively detailed, but I doubt that users of v5.1 are interested in changes that happened 1.5+ years ago in v1.3.

I think we should figure out how these files could grow and how they should be displayed. Maybe we need to customize the content extraction of the changelog, and display only the last-N versions (or up until 128 Kb). That way the input file could keep its size, and we also limit the size to the common query patterns.
